comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Lending risk-adjusted margin and purchase volumes
comparisons.peer_summary: Total risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 bps driven by higher net credit losses, while total credit card and debit card purchase volumes increased to $368.9 billion and $557.0 billion respectively, reflecting higher consumer spending.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America reported that higher net credit losses were a primary driver of margin compression in 2024, reflecting similar credit performance headwinds in consumer lending. Citi explicitly states it expects elevated net credit loss rates in 2025 consistent with 2024 levels, particularly in Branded Cards. BAC reports its risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 basis points in 2024 primarily driven by higher net credit losses, coinciding with increased credit card purchase volumes. While Citi focuses on the forward-looking rate consistency and BAC on the resulting margin impact, both identify net credit losses as a significant negative factor for their consumer banking segments.

sentences.text: Subject to evolving macroeconomic conditions, Citi expects to continue to experience an elevated net credit loss rate for full-year 2025 in line with 2024, with higher loss rates in the first half of the year in Branded Cards and Retail Services consistent with seasonal patterns.
Citi also expects that its future ACL builds will be driven by both the macroeconomic environment and business volumes, among other factors.
Total risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 bps primarily driven by higher net credit losses, partially offset by higher net interest margin and higher net fee income.
Total credit card purchase volumes increased $5.7 billion to $368.9 billion, and debit card purchase volumes increased $29.9 billion to $557.0 billion, reflecting higher levels of consumer spending.

comparisons.peer_summary: Macroeconomic forecasts are inherently uncertain and may differ significantly from actual losses, with further information available in Note 9 to the consolidated financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Citi identifies macroeconomic conditions as a key driver for its future Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) builds, noting that future trends will be driven by the macroeconomic environment. Similarly, Goldman Sachs highlights that macroeconomic forecasts are inherently uncertain and that actual credit losses in an adverse macroeconomic environment may differ significantly from estimates. Both disclosures underscore the dependency of credit loss expectations and ACL adequacy on the trajectory and uncertainty of macroeconomic conditions, although Citi provides a specific outlook for 2025 while GS provides a general cautionary statement about forecast uncertainty.

comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase discuss the drivers of changes in their Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) in 2024. Both firms link ACL movements to the interplay of loan volume growth and macroeconomic assumptions, with Citi offering a forward-looking view on 2025 volumes/conditions and JPM explaining the historical 2024 drivers.

comparisons.peer_topic: Macroeconomic Variables and ACL Methodology Reference
comparisons.peer_summary: The ACL calculation incorporates corporate credit spreads, interest rates, and commercial real estate indices as key macroeconomic variables, with further details on the CECL methodology provided in Note 2.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and Morgan Stanley both explicitly identify macroeconomic variables as inputs into their credit loss modeling and allowance calculations. Citi notes that future ACL builds are driven by the macroeconomic environment. Morgan Stanley specifies that corporate credit spreads, interest rates, and commercial real estate indices are key macroeconomic variables used in the ACL calculation. Both disclosures establish the direct link between macroeconomic indicators and the financial measurement of credit losses, though Morgan Stanley details the specific variables used in its CECL methodology while Citi references the general impact on future builds.
